chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

It is not permissible for a terminally ill person to divorce, but he may marry. If he marries and consummates the marriage, it is valid; but if he does not consummate it until he dies in his illness, his marriage is void, she receives no dowry, and she inherits no share.

key_terms.المَرِيض: The terminally ill person (one with a deathbed illness)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage and divorce for a terminally ill person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar clarifies the status of marriage during the final illness (marad al-maut), distinguishing between consummated and unconsummated unions to determine financial rights. It establishes that while divorce is restricted to prevent hasty dissolution, the validity of marriage hinges on consummation, directly impacting the wife's entitlement to dowry (mahr) and inheritance (mirath). This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the stability of family ties during the critical period of death preparation.
